meta.title: Q-SIEVE
meta.dataMode: Real IBM AML HI-Small transactions (public dataset)
meta.simulation: Exact statevector simulator for the benchmark; real QPUs for the hardware batch.
meta.scoreDescription: Sigmoid-scaled angle-kernel SVC decision score. Not a calibrated probability of financial crime.
meta.fixtureSelection: 12 real flagged windows selected across the score range from a 3000-window test pool. Selection does not affect the benchmark metrics.
caveats: Public IBM AML data; labels are the dataset’s, not a bank’s ground truth.
The kernel runs on a simulator for the benchmark and on real hardware for the degradation report; no quantum advantage is claimed.
Near-zero net flow and near-threshold transfers also occur in legitimate businesses.

features.label: Activity vs baseline
features.description: Transactions this window divided by the account’s own median window size. High = a burst of activity.

features.label: Average transfer
features.description: Gross volume divided by transaction count, in USD (15 currencies normalised).

features.label: Inbound share (count)
features.description: Share of transactions that are credits into the account.

features.label: Inbound share (value)
features.description: Share of gross value that flows in rather than out.

features.label: Net ÷ gross flow
features.description: Signed net change over gross flow. Near zero means money largely passes through.

features.label: Mean time between tx
features.description: Average gap between consecutive transactions in the window.

features.label: Distinct counterparties
features.description: Number of distinct accounts transacted with this window.

features.label: Near the 10k line
features.description: Share of transfers just under the 10,000 USD reporting threshold (9k–10k).

policy.closureRule: Only clear-eligible windows may be auto-cleared; escalated or retained windows stay open.

hardware.status: Run on real quantum hardware (full 1,024 shots)
hardware.note: Bandwidth-tuned kernel (c=0.1, 6 qubits) on three real QPUs, 1,024 shots each. The scores SCATTER 0.183 / 0.265 / 0.395 around the 0.231 simulator — IBM lands ABOVE the noiseless sim, which is impossible for a real signal. The tuned model is near-degenerate (every point a support vector), so tiny readout noise is amplified into big swings: noise-dominated, not a result. The reliable hardware validation is the robust c=1 config (Garnet and IBM 0.111→0.111, Q50 0.111→0.100, drift under 0.02).

xgboost.note: Real tuned XGBoost (GridSearchCV), not a substitute.

evaluation.protocol: Real IBM AML HI-Small. Identical 12 features, 70/30 split (seed 0), train capped at 200 for every model. Benchmark PR-AUC is mean over 3 seeds.
caveats: Honest result: the naive quantum kernel (0.125) trails tuned classical — until the bandwidth is tuned to c≈0.1, where it reaches ~0.18, statistically level with the tuned tree (a tie within noise, not a win).
The optimal bandwidth is DERIVED analytically (c = 1/√(n·d) = 0.083), not found by trial-and-error — and it lands on the measured peak.

On real hardware the ROBUST c=1 config is the reliable validation (near-zero drift, 3 vendors). The aggressive tuned config runs but its score is noise-dominated (scatter 0.18–0.40) — a fragility finding, not a win.
